item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 251711
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Fri Sep 25 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, located a few hundred miles southwest of Cabo Corrientes,
Mexico, on Hurricane Odalys, located well west-southwest of the
southern tip of Baja California, and on Hurricane Nolo, located
a couple hundred miles south of the Big Island of Hawaii.

South of the Gulf of Tehuantepec:
An area of low pressure is expected to form in a day or so to the
south of the Gulf of Tehuantepec. Afterward, environmental
conditions appear favorable for gradual development, and a tropical
depression is expected to form late this weekend or early next week
while the system moves slowly west-northwestward to northwestward,
parallel to the coast of southern and southwestern Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...50 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Well East-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
A broad area of low pressure is forecast to form about 1000 miles
east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands over the weekend.
Environmental conditions appear favorable for gradual development of
this system, and a tropical depression could form early next week.
The system is forecast to move generally northeastward, remaining
well east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

$$
Forecaster Roberts

MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...951 MB...28.09 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM PDT (2100 UTC), the center of Hurricane Odalys was located 
near latitude 18.3 North, longitude 123.6 West. Odalys is moving 
toward the north-northeast near 5 mph (7 km/h). A northward motion 
is expected tonight through Saturday, followed by a turn toward the 
northeast on Sunday. An eastward to southeastward motion is 
forecast early next week.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 125 mph (205 km/h) with higher
gusts. Odalys is a category 3 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson
Hurricane Wind Scale. A weakening trend is forecast beginning
tonight and continuing through early next week.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
(205 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 951 mb (28.09 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Reinhart

item.title: Hurricane Odalys Forecast Discussion Number 23
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Fri Sep 25 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 251447
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Odalys Discussion Number  23
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP162026
800 AM PDT Fri Sep 25 2026
 
Odalys has rapidly intensified this morning, and the conventional
satellite presentation consists of a 30 nmi 5 deg C irregular eye 
with inner core convection cloud tops of -80 deg C.  The wind 
pattern aloft has improved since yesterday, with apparent dual 
outflow channels located over the northeast and southwest quadrants. 
The Dvorak intensity estimate from TAFB and the UW-CIMSS objective 
intensity techniques support holding the initial intensity at 115 
kt.
 
Over the weekend, Odalys should encounter a progressively 
inhibiting surrounding atmospheric environment and decreasing 
oceanic temperatures.  Accordingly, the cyclone should gradually 
weaken, lose its organized convection late this weekend, and become 
a post-tropical cyclone while maintaining gale-force winds.  The NHC 
intensity forecast is bumped slightly upward due to the rapid 
intensification period, and is just above the HFIP HCCA and near 
the Google DeepMind ensemble guidance.
 
Odalys' initial motion is estimated to be north-northeastward, or 
030/5 kt.  By early Saturday, the cyclone should turn northward, 
moving in the southerly steering flow provided by an amplifying 
mid- to upper-level tropospheric trough approaching the west coast 
of the U.S. and the Baja California peninsula.  By early next week, 
an increasing influence from Hurricane Polo's horizontal wind field 
is expected to induce a relatively sharp turn eastward while the 
cyclone continues to weaken.  By day 4, Odalys is forecast to 
turn southeastward within the southwestern peripheral flow of 
Polo and reduce in forward speed.  Very few adjustments were made 
to the previous advisory, and the new track forecast lies close to 
the better-performing HCCA and GDMI aids.
 
Moisture from both Odalys and Polo will be carried a long distance
into the southwestern U.S. this weekend and early next week, and may
indirectly contribute to a heavy rainfall and flash flood threat in
the region.  See products issued by the Weather Prediction Center
for more information.

item.title: Hurricane Polo Public Advisory Number 20
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Fri Sep 25 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 251449
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Polo Advisory Number  20
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
800 AM MST Fri Sep 25 2026
 
...POLO IS AN EXTREMELY POWERFUL CATEGORY 5 HURRICANE...
...INTERESTS IN BAJA CALIFORNIA SUR SHOULD MONITOR ITS PROGRESS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM MST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.1N 108.5W
ABOUT 290 MI...470 KM SW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
ABOUT 410 MI...660 KM SSE OF CABO SAN LUCAS MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...180 MPH...285 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 270 DEGREES AT 12 MPH...19 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...900 MB...26.58 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in Baja California Sur should closely monitor the progress
of this system. Watches could be required for a portion of the area
as early as Saturday.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM MST (1500 UTC), the eye of Hurricane Polo was located 
near latitude 17.1 North, longitude 108.5 West. Polo is moving 
toward the west near 12 mph (19 km/h), and this motion is expected 
to continue through today. A gradual turn to the northwest and north 
is forecast on Saturday and Sunday, followed by a northeastward 
motion on Monday. On the forecast track, Polo is expected to 
approach Baja California Sur early next week.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 180 mph (285 km/h) with higher
gusts. Polo is a category 5 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson
Hurricane Wind Scale. Fluctuations in intensity are possible today,
but some weakening is expected over the weekend. Polo is forecast to
approach Baja California Sur as a strong hurricane early next week.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 40 miles (65 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 115 miles
(185 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 900 mb (26.58 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Polo can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP2 and WMO header WTPZ42 KNHC.
 
RAINFALL: Polo is expected to produce rainfall totals of 4 to 8
inches with maximum amounts of 10 inches across portions of Baja
California Sur. This rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding
and mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated
with Polo, please see the National Weather Service Storm Total
Rainfall Graphic available at
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf
 
SURF: Swells generated by Polo will continue affecting the coast of
southwestern Mexico during the next couple of days. Swells will
spread northward along the coast of west-central Mexico and the Baja
California Peninsula through the weekend. These swells are likely
to cause life-threatening surf, rip currents, and coastal flooding.
Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Reinhart

item.title: Hurricane Polo Forecast Discussion Number 20
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Fri Sep 25 2026 
645 
WTPZ42 KNHC 251450
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Polo Discussion Number  20
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
800 AM MST Fri Sep 25 2026
 
After regaining Category 5 status overnight, the remarkable
satellite presentation of Polo indicates the hurricane has continued
to intensify. The eye has contracted and warmed over the past
several hours, with temperatures above 20 deg C measured inside the
eye. A thick, solid ring of deep convection surrounds the center,
with cloud tops as cold as -80 to -85 deg C. There were no
indications of a concentric eyewall structure in 0905 UTC AMSR3
passive microwave imagery. The latest UW-CIMSS ADT estimates and a
T7.5 Dvorak classification from TAFB support an initial intensity of
155 kt. A NOAA research aircraft mission is scheduled to investigate
Polo later today.
 
Polo continues moving westward (270/10 kt) along the south side of a
mid-level ridge that extends across northern Mexico. This weekend, a
deep-layer trough approaching from the west is expected to erode the
steering ridge. This will cause Polo to turn northwestward and
northward as it moves around the western side of the ridge. By
Monday, the increasing influence of the upper trough should turn
Polo northeastward toward Baja California Sur and west-central
Mexico. The global models and AI-based guidance are generally
in good agreement on this track evolution. The updated NHC track
forecast is adjusted slightly to the left of the previous one, and
is also a bit slower to come into better agreement with the latest
multi-model consensus. Overall, the NHC forecast remains on the
faster and right side of the envelope, closer to HCCA and GDMI.
Based on this prediction, watches could be required for portions of
the Baja California Peninsula as early as Saturday.
 
Based on the aforementioned AMSR3 data, an eyewall replacement cycle
(ERC) does not appear imminent. Thus, further slight strengthening
cannot be ruled out while Polo remains over very warm waters in a
weaker shear environment. The vertical wind shear is expected to
increase over the weekend, and because of this as well as the
possibility of a future ERC, the NHC intensity forecast shows a
weakening trend beginning on Saturday and continuing into next week.
Regardless, Polo is predicted to approach Baja California Sur as a
strong hurricane early next week, and interests there should closely
monitor the latest forecast updates. The NHC forecast remains on the
higher side of the intensity guidance, generally following HCCA.
Once land interaction occurs with the Baja California Peninsula and
mainland Mexico, more rapid weakening is anticipated.
 
Distant moisture from Hurricane Polo and Odalys will be transported
into the southwestern United States this weekend and early next
week, and may indirectly contribute to a heavy rainfall and flash
flood threat in the region. See products issued by the Weather
Prediction Center for more information.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Polo is forecast to approach the Baja California Peninsula early
next week as a hurricane. Interests there should closely monitor
the latest updates and ensure that they have their preparedness
plan in place. Watches could be required as early as Saturday for
portions of the area.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with Polo may begin to impact Baja
California Sur late Sunday into Monday. This rainfall may produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
